newsitem.title: USA: Total sees 12 pct capital spending rise.
newsitem.headline: Total sees 12 pct capital spending rise.

text.p: Total SA is projecting capital spending of 18 billion francs this year, up 12 percent from last year's outlays, Executive Vice President - Exploration and Production Daniel Valot told a PaineWebber conference.
He said 61 percent of the 1997 outlays will go to such upstream activities as exploration and production.
As a result, Valot said, Total expects 44 percent of its capital employed will be involved in upstream activities in 1997, up from 41 percent last year and 38 percent in 1995.
He said the portion will continue to rise over the next three years, reaching 48 percent in 2000 when the capital employed is expected to total 100 billion francs, up from 78 billion in 1995.

He said Total's production level target is now one million barrels of oil equivalent per day in 2000, noting the company now expects to reach its goal of doubling 1990 production of 273,000 barrels daily in eight years instead of the targeted 10 years.
Valot said 1996 daily production of 473,000 barrels of oil equivalent is expected to grow to 500,000 this year and 545,000 in 1998.
